clues: In 1943, actress Gene Tierney caught this disease from an overzealous fan who broke out of quarantine to meet her. She was pregnant at the time and her baby was born deaf, blind, and with severe intellectual disabilities.

Also known as third disease in the historical numbering system for classic childhood rash illnesses, this was dismissed as a harmless illness until a 1941 Australian ophthalmologist linked it to congenital cataracts and other severe birth defects, changing how science viewed prenatal viral illnesses
Characterized by a fine maculopapular rash that starts on the face, tender lymphadenopathy, and low grade fevers, this disease is rarely seen now after development of a live-attenuated vaccine

In the 1920s to 1940s, doctors deliberately infected patients with malaria to treat this disease. The high, repeating fevers caused by malaria cured the disease and then doctors used quinine to cure the patient of malaria. This discovery won a Nobel Prize in 1927
Before antibiotics, this was called the 'general paresis of the insane' causing profound dementia, delusions of grandeur and eventual paralysis
Physical exam findings can vary but often reveal pupils that constrict for near vision but not bright light and a broad-based ataxic gait

Many of this class of medications are used as herbicides becaues they can interfere with plant biosynthesis of certain amino acids such as valine and leucine. They are used to control weeds in major crops like corn, wheat, and rice.

In the 1940s, researchers testing early sulfonamide antibacterial drugs noticed patients kept passing out. Scientists discovered they could re-engineer these drugs to take advantage of this side effect, leading to first generation pills like tolbutamide

This class of medications bind to and close ATP-sensitive K+ channels on the cell membrane of pancreatic beta cells, ultimately increasing secretion of insulin. Due to the risk of hypoglycemia and the availability of alternative options, these are no longer first line options but might be used when cost is a barrier
A natural pesticide produced by some plants such as kola nut, camellia sinensis, ilex paraguariensis among others, this naturally occuring compound was first isolated in 1820 by a German chemist
This primarily acts as an adenosine receptor antagonist, targeting A1 and A2A adenosine receptors, which are found throughout the body in the brain, heart, blood vessels, kidneys, and immune cells

One of the most widely consumed psychoactive substances in the world, this substance does not actually provide the body with energy. Instead, it temporarily interferes with the brain's signaling of fatigue
